arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Srinivasan argued the statute streamlines removal of reentered aliens.
He stated Congress did not intend to exempt current illegal residents.
Mr. Gossett argued the statute applies only prospectively.
He cited ordinary tools of statutory construction to support his view.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the scope of a 1996 immigration statute. The core issue is whether the law applies to aliens already in the country. the side that brought the case argues the law applies only to future reentries. the opposing side argues the law applies to all current removals. The Court must interpret the statute's effective date.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the reach of immigration removal statutes. It determines which aliens face expedited removal. It clarifies the effective date of federal laws. It impacts the rights of non-citizens in the country. It shapes future legislative drafting for immigration policy.
